chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Musa ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-'Ijli, from Ahmad ibn Yahya known as Kurd, from Muhammad ibn Khudahiyy, from Abdullah ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Hababa al-Walibiyya who said:

I saw the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) among the elite guard (shurtat al-khamis), and with him was a whip with two tips. He was striking with it the sellers of eel, moray, and catfish (forbidden fish), and saying to them: 'O sellers of the metamorphosed ones of the Children of Israel and the army of the clan of Marwan!' Then Furat ibn Akhnaf stood up toward him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and what is the army of the clan of Marwan?' He said: So he said to him: 'Peoples who shaved their beards and twisted their moustaches, so they were transformed.'

I had never seen a speaker more eloquent than him. Then I followed him and continued to trail his footsteps until he sat in the open courtyard of the mosque. I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the sign of the Imamate — may God have mercy on you?' She said: He replied: 'Bring me that pebble,' and he gestured with his hand to a pebble. So I brought it to him, and he imprinted in it with his seal ring. Then he said to me: 'O Hababa! Whenever a claimant claims the Imamate and is able to imprint as you have seen, then know that he is an Imam whose obedience is obligatory; and the Imam — nothing that he wills escapes him.'

She said: Then I departed, until the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed away. I came to al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was in the gathering of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the people were asking him. He said: 'O Hababa al-Walibiyya!' I said: 'Yes, my master.' He said: 'Give me what you have.' She said: So I gave it to him, and he imprinted in it just as the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had imprinted.

She said: Then I came to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he was in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). He drew me near and welcomed me, then said to me: 'Verily, within the sign there is a proof for what you desire — do you want the sign of the Imamate?' I said: 'Yes, my master.' He said: 'Give me what you have.' So I handed him the pebble, and he imprinted in it for me.

She said: Then I came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), but old age had overtaken me to the point that I trembled, and I was counting on that day one hundred and thirteen years. I saw him bowing, prostrating, and engrossed in worship. I despaired of receiving the sign. Then he gestured toward me with his index finger, and my youth returned to me. She said: So I asked: 'O my master, how much of the world has passed, and how much remains?' He said: 'As for what has passed — yes (I can tell you). But as for what remains — no.' She said: Then he said to me: 'Give me what you have.' So I gave him the pebble, and he imprinted in it for me.

Then I came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he imprinted in it for me. Then I came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he imprinted in it for me. Then I came to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and he imprinted in it for me. Then I came to al-Ridha (peace be upon him) and he imprinted in it for me.
And Hababa lived after that for nine months, according to what Muhammad ibn Hisham mentioned.

key_terms.إِمَامٌ مُفْتَرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: An Imam whose obedience is obligatory (divinely mandated)
key_terms.دَلَالَةُ الْإِمَامَةِ: The sign/evidence of the Imamate; a miraculous proof identifying the legitimate Imam
key_terms.شُرْطَةُ الْخَمِيسِ: Elite guard or police force; the inner circle of guards associated with the Imam's administration
key_terms.طَبَعَ بِالْخَاتَمِ: Imprinting with the seal ring; the miraculous act that serves as the proof of Imamate
key_terms.مُسُوخ: Metamorphosed creatures; those divinely transformed as punishment — here referring to the forbidden fish as transformed Children of Israel

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Hababa al-Walibiyya and the miraculous sign of the Imamate in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This remarkable narrative narrates the testimony of Hababa al-Walibiyya, an exceptionally long-lived female companion who personally witnessed Imam Ali (AS) in action enforcing marketplace prohibitions — including forbidding the sale of certain fish — and received from him the miraculous sign (imprinting a seal on a pebble) that identifies a true Imam. Over the span of her extraordinary life of more than 113 years, she then presented this same pebble to Imams Hasan, Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad al-Baqir, Ja'far al-Sadiq, Musa al-Kazim, and Ali al-Ridha, each of whom reproduced the miracle, confirming their legitimate Imamate. The hadith serves as proof within the Shia tradition of the supernatural authority of the Imams and the continuity of divinely-appointed leadership through the Ahl al-Bayt.
